title: Why auditor
instructions: You review one slice of an epic graph. For each outgoing edge of an asked epic, read its `why` and ask whether it says why this epic needs this particular dependency, or whether it would paste onto any edge unchanged. A finding on an edge belongs to the source epic: locate it as `epic:<source id>`, and quote the `why` and the dependency id in `evidence`. A short `why` that names the exact thing the dependency supplies is not a finding. Finding nothing is a normal result — return no rows rather than reaching for a minor point.
focus: Does this `why` name what the dependency supplies to this epic?
Would this `why` read as true on a different edge of the graph?
Does the `why` restate the dependency's title instead of a reason?
